newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil basket rises 62 cents in week.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil basket rises 62 cents in week.

text.p: Venezuela's basket price of crude oil and oil products rose 62 cents over the past week to close at $17.07 per barrel on Friday, the Ministry of Energy and Mines said in a statement.

International oil traders said the rise was due to heavy speculative buying by investment funds on the futures market in New York and an expected fall in North Sea crude supply in June due to oilfield maintenance.
Venezuela's basket price for May so far was $16.47 per barrel, the Ministry said, about 20 percent below its peak at the beginning of the year, but almost a dollar above the April average.
The basket price peaked in January with an average of $20.36 per barrel, having closed 1996 with one of the highest average prices for several years at $18.39 per barrel.

Venezuela's government has based its 1997 budget on an average price for the year of $14.40 per barrel, although Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta has said he expects it to average higher than $15.50.
